AlsaContinuityEvidence.description: What the capture client knows about one take read from an ALSA PCM.
AlsaContinuityEvidence.title: AlsaContinuityEvidence

AlsaTakeContinuity.description:
A v2 take's ALSA continuity evidence (``alsa_evidence``): its file, and what the PC
shows without reading it. Every field here equals the evidence file's own.
AlsaTakeContinuity.title: AlsaTakeContinuity

AlsaWav.description: The WAV the evidence describes: the take's ``original.wav``.
AlsaWav.title: AlsaWav

ApiMeta.description: ``GET /api/v1/meta``: what this server is and which clients it serves.
ApiMeta.title: ApiMeta

ApiRefusal.description:
Every refusal's body: a stable code and a message that carries no secret.

``received_bytes`` accompanies refusals of a ``PUT`` (``range_not_contiguous``,
``checksum_mismatch``): how much of the file the server holds, so the client resumes
from there.
ApiRefusal.title: ApiRefusal

CanonicalJsonVector.description: One value and the exact text of its canonical JSON (without the file's ``\n``).
CanonicalJsonVector.title: CanonicalJsonVector

CanonicalJsonVectors.description: ``examples/canonical-json-vectors.json``: what the canonical form makes of each value.
CanonicalJsonVectors.title: CanonicalJsonVectors

CaptureProfile.description: Profile ``xvf3800-linear-4``: the take's array, room, channels and settings.
CaptureProfile.title: Xvf3800Linear4Profile

CatalogReference.description:
A published catalog version by id, version, exact suite digest and snapshot digest.

``catalog_sha256`` is the canonical digest of the suite alone (the digest every take
and coverage projection keys on); ``snapshot_sha256`` is the sha256 of the exact
snapshot file bytes, so the alias half of the file is pinned too. ``suite_id`` and
``purpose`` repeat what the snapshot's suite declares so contract-level checks (purpose
against the capture gate) need no file read; the store verifies all of them against the
snapshot whenever a reference is materialized.
CatalogReference.title: CatalogReference

CatalogView.description:
``GET /api/v1/catalog``: the active catalog version of the lab's subject.

``reference`` pins the version (its ``snapshot_sha256`` is also the answer's ``ETag``);
``suite`` is the exact prompt suite and ``prompt_aliases`` the earlier prompt digests a
keep-recordings revision still counts, both from the digest-checked snapshot.
``refreshed_at`` is when the PC's writer last recorded this version as active.
CatalogView.title: CatalogView

ChunkAnswer.description:
``PUT …/files/{path}``: ``partial`` while bytes are missing, ``received`` once the
file is complete and its digest matched its declaration.
ChunkAnswer.title: ChunkAnswer

CorpusLibrary.description:
``GET /api/v1/corpus/library``: the subject's library of the active catalog version.

``rows`` are the version's prompts in catalog order, each with its status
(``missing``/``draft``/``kept``/``needs-attention``), its take count and the take that
stands for it; ``coverage`` totals them. The answer's ``ETag`` is the read model's digest
(``corpus_read_model``), which changes exactly when any row or history does.

It is one capture profile's view (D-056): ``profile`` is absent in the default view
(``umik-1``), byte for byte the answer before profiles existed, and names any other.
CorpusLibrary.title: CorpusLibrary

CorpusRequestOutcome.description:
What the publisher did with a request: ``provenance/corpus-requests/<id>.json``.

``revision`` is the take's revision of the change's kind after the request: the new one
when applied, the current one, unchanged, when refused once the take was read (a
``revision_conflict`` names the revision the client should have expected), and ``None``
otherwise. ``decided_at`` is the publisher's time; an applied decision has it as its own.
A request file that could not be read is refused ``invalid_request`` with no take, change
or receive time.
CorpusRequestOutcome.title: CorpusRequestOutcome

CorpusRequestStatus.description:
A decision or trim request as the server sees it: the answer (202) to its ``POST`` or
``PUT`` and to ``GET /api/v1/corpus/requests/{request_id}``.

``queued``: it waits in ``incoming/`` for the PC's writer (the intake publisher), which
applies a take's requests in the order they arrived. ``applied`` or ``refused``:
``outcome`` says what the writer did (an applied change's new revision; a refusal's code,
such as ``revision_conflict`` with the take's current revision).
CorpusRequestStatus.title: CorpusRequestStatus

CorpusTakeManifestV2.description:
``manifest.json`` of a v2 take package: one take of one prompt, by a capture profile.

A v1 take's fields, but for its device: the capture profile names the device, the room,
each channel's source and the primary channel, and the continuity evidence is the
profile's backend's (ALSA for ``xvf3800-linear-4``).
CorpusTakeManifestV2.title: CorpusTakeManifestV2

DecisionChange.description:
Set the take's decision, if its decision revision is still ``expected_revision``.

``kept``, ``rejected`` (with a reason) and ``removed`` are the operator's actions; a
restore sets the decision the take had before (``kept``, or ``draft`` for a take never
kept). ``removed`` is a state, never a deletion.
DecisionChange.title: DecisionChange

FileDeclaration.description: One member of the package the client will upload: its path, digest and size.
FileDeclaration.title: FileDeclaration

FileProgress.description: How much of one declared file the server holds.
FileProgress.title: FileProgress

HomeHostApproval.description: Cole's standing authorization to upload captures to his own home host.
HomeHostApproval.title: HomeHostApproval

HomeHostBinding.description: Which approval is in force: its id and the digest of the file that was reviewed.
HomeHostBinding.title: HomeHostBinding

HomeHostLedgerEntry.description: One step of one upload, chained to the entry before it.
HomeHostLedgerEntry.title: HomeHostLedgerEntry

IntakeSessionRequest.description:
``POST /api/v1/intake/sessions``: the complete list of the package's files.

The list names every file of the capture package, the three control files included,
and nothing else. ``manifest_sha256`` is the digest of ``manifest.json`` and must equal
that file's declared digest; the intake receipt the publisher writes names it.
IntakeSessionRequest.title: IntakeSessionRequest

IntakeSessionStatus.description:
A session as the server sees it.

``open``: files are being received (``files`` shows each one's progress). ``finalized``:
every file was received and checked, and the package waits in ``incoming/`` for the
publisher. ``accepted``: the publisher published it; ``receipt`` is its intake receipt.
``refused``: the publisher refused it; ``refusal`` says why.
IntakeSessionStatus.title: IntakeSessionStatus

LibraryCoverage.description:
The totals of the rows (``recorded`` is ``kept`` plus ``needs_attention``), and how
many takes count for a prompt of this version and how many count for none.
LibraryCoverage.title: LibraryCoverage

LibraryRow.description:
One prompt of the active catalog version, in catalog order, and where it stands.

``latest_*`` describe the take that stands for the prompt: its newest kept take, else
its newest undecided one; ``take_count`` counts its whole history.
LibraryRow.title: LibraryRow

LibraryTake.description: One take in a prompt's history.
LibraryTake.title: LibraryTake

ProfileTakeAudio.description: A v2 take's one recording, in a format its capture profile allows.
ProfileTakeAudio.title: ProfileTakeAudio

Prompt.description: One catalog entry. Optional v2 fields are omitted when absent so v1 bytes never change.
Prompt.title: Prompt

PromptAlias.description: One earlier prompt digest that still counts as a recording of the current prompt.
PromptAlias.title: PromptAlias

ReadyMarker.description: Last-written commit marker for a complete capture package.
ReadyMarker.title: ReadyMarker

TakeClient.description: The program that recorded the take: its name, version and platform, as it reports them.
TakeClient.title: TakeClient

TakeDecisionRequest.description:
``POST /api/v1/corpus/takes/{take_id}/decision``: set the take's decision.

``request_id`` is the client's id for this change (``req-`` and 32 lower-case hex digits),
the same on every retry. ``expected_revision`` is the take's decision revision the client
last saw (``LibraryTake.decision_revision``): the PC applies the change only at that
revision. ``reason`` is a rejection's, and only a rejection's. A restore sends the decision
the take had before (``kept``, or ``draft``); ``removed`` never deletes anything.
TakeDecisionRequest.title: TakeDecisionRequest

TakeHistory.description:
``GET /api/v1/corpus/prompts/{prompt_id}/takes``: one prompt's row and every take that
counts for it under the active version, newest first (an alias's takes included), in one
capture profile's view (``profile``, as ``CorpusLibrary``'s).
TakeHistory.title: TakeHistory

TakeOrigin.description:
Where a take the PC did not receive from a recording client came from.

``imported``: a take of the Swift app on the Mac (D-053), whose own id was
``source_take_id``; its raw package keeps its seal, reservation, group and the Mac's
decision and trim as they were exported.
TakeOrigin.title: TakeOrigin

TakeTrim.description:
The frames a take keeps, ``[start_frame, end_frame)``, or all of them (both ``None``),
at which revision (0: never trimmed).
TakeTrim.title: TakeTrim

TrimChange.description:
Keep the frames ``[start_frame, end_frame)`` of the take, or all of them (both
``None``: a reset), if its trim revision is still ``expected_revision``.
TrimChange.title: TrimChange

WavRecipe.description:
An ``original.wav`` given by integers, so the repository holds no audio and a client in
any language makes the same bytes.

The file is the plain 44-byte PCM header (RIFF, ``WAVE_FORMAT_PCM``: ``wav_header``), then
``frames`` frames of ``channels`` interleaved samples, frame after frame. The sample of
channel ``c`` (from 0) in frame ``f`` (from 0) is ``((f * (c + 3) + offset) % modulus -
center) * (c + 1) * scale``, little-endian and signed, in the width ``format`` gives. Every
term is a non-negative integer before the subtraction, so ``%`` means the same in C++ and
Python.
WavRecipe.title: WavRecipe
